map.输入随机尿或晨尿的白蛋白浓度与肌酐浓度，计算尿白蛋白肌酐比（UACR，单位 mg: Enter the albumin and creatinine concentrations in a random or morning urine sample to compute the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR, mg/g) with grading into normal, microalbuminuria and macroalbuminuria, for early kidney damage screening.
map.输入尿白蛋白（mg/L 或 mg/dL）与肌酐（mmol/L 或 mg/dL）: Enter urine albumin (mg/L or mg/dL) and creatinine (mmol/L or mg/dL)
map.自动按单位换算并计算 UACR（mg/g）: Automatically converts units and computes UACR (mg/g)
map.输出分级：正常 / 微量白蛋白尿 / 大量白蛋白尿: Outputs a grade: normal / microalbuminuria / macroalbuminuria
map.附各分级的临床意义说明: Includes the clinical meaning of each grade
map.纯前端计算，数据不上传: Pure front-end computation, data not uploaded
map.体检解读：把化验单数值换算成 ACR: Interpreting checkups: convert lab values to ACR
map.慢病随访：糖尿病、高血压患者的肾损伤监测: Chronic disease follow-up: kidney damage monitoring for diabetes and hypertension
map.科普学习：理解微量白蛋白尿的意义: Education: understanding the meaning of microalbuminuria
map.选择白蛋白与肌酐的单位: Choose the units for albumin and creatinine
map.填入尿白蛋白浓度与肌酐浓度: Enter the urine albumin and creatinine concentrations
map.查看分级与对应说明: View the grade and its explanation
map.UACR 用随机尿即可，受饮水影响比单次尿蛋白小: UACR works with a random urine sample and is less affected by fluid intake than a single urine protein measure
map.单位一定要选对，mg/L 与 mg/dL 差 10 倍: Units must be right—mg/L and mg/dL differ by a factor of 10
map.微量白蛋白尿通常 30~300 mg/g，>300 为大量: Microalbuminuria is typically 30~300 mg/g; >300 is macroalbuminuria
map.结果仅供解读参考，确诊需结合临床与多次复查: Results are for interpretation reference only; diagnosis needs clinical context and repeat testing
map.慢性肾病 (CKD) CGA 分期管理器: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) CGA Staging Manager
map.ACR 和 24 小时尿蛋白有什么区别？: What's the difference between ACR and 24-hour urine protein?
map.ACR 用随机尿估算，方便筛查；24 小时尿更准但麻烦，二者互补。: ACR estimates from a random urine sample, convenient for screening; 24-hour urine is more accurate but cumbersome—the two complement each other.
map.单位选错会怎样？: What happens if the unit is wrong?
map.肌酐单位 mg/dL 与 mmol/L 差约 88 倍，选错结果会严重偏差。: Creatinine units mg/dL and mmol/L differ by about 88×, so the wrong choice badly skews the result.
